newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo January m/m RPI up 1.4 percent - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo January m/m RPI up 1.4 percent - agency.

text.p: Yugoslav retail prices were up 1.4 percent in January compared to the previous month, the official Tanjug news agency said on Tuesday.
"(Retail) prices stabilised in January," Mirjana Rankovic, assistant director to the Federal Statistics Office, was quoted as saying.
"According to statistical analysis, monthly inflation in January this year saw the lowest increase compared to the last couple of previous years.
"Such a monthly rise corresponds to 20 percent annual inflation," she said.
Year-on-year January RPI increase was 37.7 percent.
Industrial products RPI increased less than two percent. Prices of food products were up 1.7 percent and non-food products were up only 1.1 percent against December.
"But seasonal factors pushed prices of agricultural products up 6.6 percent this month," she added.
The retail price index (RPI), used for measuring inflation, was 1.3 percent up in Serbia and 1.8 percent up in Montenegro compared to the prevous month.
In December last year, monthly RPI was 4.4 percent and year-on-year change stood at 57.8 percent.
